data.name: Cob
data.gender_notes: Cob is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old English ‘cobbe’ meaning ‘rock, stone’. In Old English literature, Cobbe was a nickname for Thrithneard, a character in the Anglo-Saxon epic poem Beowulf. The name carries the symbolism of strength, resilience, and steadfastness. The name Cob carries the meaning “Rock, Stone” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Cob usually hope their child will grow to embody rock, stone and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of strength and resilience in the face of life's challenges.
data.etymology: Cob belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Rock, Stone.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cob total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
